title: fix(desktop): a sidecar read error never mints a new assetId (NIW2-568)
body:
## Problem

`LibraryVault.sidecar()` returned `{}` on **any** read or JSON error. `ensureIdentity()` then treated the item as a legacy one, minted a new `assetId`, and the next write persisted it. A momentary EIO/EACCES (external drive), a sidecar truncated by a crash, or an evicted file in a Google Drive/OneDrive folder silently lost the item's title, tags, edit links and cloud association.

## Fix

- **Only `ENOENT` means "no sidecar"** (a real legacy item: still minted and persisted as before).
- Any other read error throws `SidecarUnavailableError("unreadable")`. A sidecar that reads but is not a JSON object (truncated, empty, `null`, array) throws `SidecarUnavailableError("corrupt")` and is copied to `<id>.json.corrupt-<ts>` once per session (same idea as `quarantine()` in `tag-repository.ts`; the original is never touched).
- `describe()` catches it and **still lists the item**, with the new optional `LocalRecording.metadataIssue` (`"unreadable" | "corrupt"`), title from the file name, and a stand-in `assetId` (`unreadable:<fileId>`, never persisted). I added this field because none of the existing axes fit: `availability` (`local-unavailable`/`unverified`) describes where the bytes live, and `unverified` is never set anywhere. The Library card/row shows a second line ("Metadata unreadable · changes are paused until it reads again", en + es).
- `writeMeta` / `writeMetaLocked` read through the same path, so **every write is refused** (rename, tags, backfill, editor-opened stamp, content hash cache) until a later read succeeds. Nothing is cached: the next list simply reads again and the item recovers its real id, title and tags.
- `compose-library`: an unreadable local file is claimed through the catalog's `lastSeenLocalId`, so the cloud association is **kept** (previously a readable vault with no `assetId` match would clear it) and the item reads `local-unavailable` as ONE item with the cloud title, not a duplicate.
- Test seam: `new LibraryVault(dir, reader?)` with a `VaultReader { readText }` (default is `fs.readFile`), so EIO/EACCES are injected deterministically.

## Caller audit

| Caller | Assumed "error = empty"? | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LibraryVault.ensureIdentity` (via `describe`/`list`) | Yes, this was the bug | Throws; `describe` returns the degraded item; nothing minted or written |
| `LibraryVault.writeMetaLocked` (merge-read before every write) | Yes: merging into `{}` would erase the file | Throws before `atomicWriteFile`; sidecar untouched |
| `rename`, `markOpenedInEditor` | via `writeMeta` | Rejected with `SidecarUnavailableError`; the renderer already catches rename errors (`errorRename` toast) and `markOpenedInEditor` is fire-and-forget |
| `backfill` (+ renderer `heal-orphan-metadata.ts` / `use-orphan-heal.ts`) | via `writeMeta` | `writeMeta` runs first, so it throws before the thumbnail is written. Renderer: `isOrphan` now skips items with `metadataIssue`, so no needless decode/IPC loop |
| `ensureContentHash` | Yes (`sidecar()` result used for the cache check) | Throws; `LibraryService.removeLocalCopy` already turns that into `hash-unknown` |
| `LibraryVault.removeLocalCopy` | Deleted the media **before** `writeMeta`, so with an unreadable sidecar the file would go without its marker | Now reads the sidecar first; throws before `rm`. Covered by a test. (The service path also stops earlier: the stand-in `assetId` has no cloud entry, so the policy returns `no-cloud-copy`.) |
| `LibraryVault.remove` (user delete) | n/a | Intentional destructive delete; unchanged. The `.corrupt-*` copy stays in `.kaipu/` |
| `tag-repository.ts` `importLegacy` (Phase 1 string tags) | Yes (`sidecar(...).tags`) | Per-item `SidecarUnavailableError` is caught: that item's sidecar is left untouched and its (never released) Phase 1 tags are not imported. Trade-off: refusing the whole import would disable tags for the vault over one bad file |
| `tag-repository.ts` `assign` / `remove` | via `writeMeta` / `list()` | `assign` rejects for a degraded item; `remove` iterates `list()` where degraded items have `tagIds: []`, so they are skipped (a dangling id to a tombstoned tag stays in that sidecar; harmless, ids are filtered on assign) |
| `library-service.ts` `list` / `removeLocalCopy` | consumes `describe` | Degraded items flow through `composeLibrary`; remove-local-copy blocked as above |
| `compose-library.ts` | Joined only by `assetId` and cleared `lastSeenLocalId` for an unmatched local | Handles `metadataIssue` (see Fix); two new tests |
| `screenshot-save.ts` | `writeImage` first, `writeMeta` after | On overwrite it now checks `vault.sidecar(id)` **before** replacing the PNG, so a refused save leaves the old image. New ids (ENOENT) are unaffected |
| `recording-writer.ts` finalize | new id, `writeMeta` then `describe` | A missing sidecar is ENOENT → unchanged. A pre-existing unreadable one throws into the existing `takeBack` path. No change needed |
| `gif-save.ts`, `stranded-recordings.ts` | new ids via `writeMeta` | Same: ENOENT unchanged; a failure hits the existing cleanup/`failed` paths. No change needed |
| `readCursorTrack` | `catch → null` | A different file (`<id>.cursor.json`), read-only, no identity or write follows; null only disables auto-zoom. Left as is |
| `video-edit-session.ts` `readExportedSavedAt`, `edit-project-probe.ts` | `catch → null` | They read `<id>.edit.meta.json`, not the item sidecar; null means "not exported" (the safe side, as documented there). Out of scope |
| `index.ts` `openSavedScreenshot` | `describe` | Works with a degraded item (read-only) |
| `isCloudUploadEligible` | n/a | Returns false for an item with `metadataIssue` (no upload exists yet in main; this keeps a future one from uploading a stand-in id) |

## Test evidence

Run in `apps/kaipu-record` (after `bun install --frozen-lockfile`):

- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run` → **309 files, 2972 tests passed** (includes the new ones)
- `bun run check-types` → node + web clean
- `bun run lint` → 0 errors (17 pre-existing warnings, none in touched code)
- `oxfmt --check .` → all files formatted; `packages/i18n` tests → 22 passed

New tests: `library-vault.sidecar-read.test.ts` (EIO and EACCES via the reader seam; a real `chmod 000` case, skipped on Windows/root; truncated JSON, empty file, `[]`, `null`; one `.corrupt-*` copy across instances; valid JSON keeps the id; ENOENT still mints; `removeLocalCopy` keeps the media), plus cases in `compose-library.test.ts`, `tag-repository.test.ts` and `use-orphan-heal.test.ts`. Error-path tests assert the sidecar is byte-identical and no extra file is created.

Not run, by instruction: the Playwright/Electron E2E suite and the `/verify` screenshot flow (both need the real app).

Refs NIW2-568 https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-568

## How to test it yourself

1. Use a vault with a recording that has a title and tags. Note its title.
2. `chmod 000 <vault>/.kaipu/<id>.json`, then refresh the Library. The item is still listed, title from the file name, with "Metadata unreadable · changes are paused…". Rename and tag edits fail with their error toast. `cat` the file after `chmod 644` (step 3): it is unchanged (no new `assetId`).
3. `chmod 644 <vault>/.kaipu/<id>.json` and refresh. The original title and tags are back, same `assetId`.
4. Truncate a sidecar: `head -c 40 <id>.json > t && mv t <id>.json`. Refresh: the item is listed as unreadable, `.kaipu/<id>.json.corrupt-<timestamp>` appears (once, however many refreshes), and `<id>.json` still holds the truncated bytes (no new id). Restore it from the `.corrupt-*` copy or the pre-truncation backup and refresh to confirm recovery.
5. Delete a sidecar entirely and refresh: the item gets a new id as before (the legacy path), no error.
